bank.q: She is not used to ___ spicy food.

articles.title: The Lost Phone
body: Budi cannot find his phone. He looks on the table, in his bag and under the bed, but it is not there.
He asks his sister, "Have you seen my phone?" She says, "No, but I can call it." She calls his number and they hear a sound from the kitchen.
The phone is next to the rice cooker. Budi laughs. "I used it to check a recipe this morning," he says. Now he always puts it in the same place.

qs.q: Where did they find the phone?
How did they find it?
opts: They saw it on the table

qs.q: What does Budi do now?
opts: He puts it in the same place

articles.title: A Rainy Saturday
body: It rains all day on Saturday, so Maya stays at home. She wears a warm sweater and makes a cup of hot chocolate.
First, she cleans her room. Then she reads a book for two hours. In the afternoon, she calls her grandmother and they talk about old photos.
In the evening, Maya cooks noodles for her family. Everyone eats together and watches a movie. It is a quiet but happy day.

qs.q: Why does Maya stay at home?
What does she do in the afternoon?
How is the day?

articles.title: Ordering Coffee in English
body: Tom is a tourist in Jakarta. He enters a small cafe and wants to order coffee. The barista smiles and says, "Hello! What would you like?"
Tom says, "A medium latte, please." The barista asks, "For here or to go?" Tom answers, "To go, please." Then he asks, "How much is it?"
The latte costs forty thousand rupiah. Tom pays with cash and says, "Thank you!" The barista says, "You are welcome. Have a nice day!"

qs.q: What does Tom order?
Does Tom drink it in the cafe?
How does Tom pay?

articles.title: Why Breakfast Matters
body: Many people skip breakfast because they are in a hurry or do not feel hungry in the morning. However, nutrition experts often call breakfast the most important meal of the day.

After a night of sleep, your body needs energy. A good breakfast, such as eggs, fruit or whole grain bread, gives you fuel for the morning. Students who eat breakfast usually concentrate better in class.
You do not need a big meal. Even a small bowl of oatmeal or a banana with some nuts is better than nothing. The key is to eat something healthy before the busy day begins.

qs.q: Why do many people skip breakfast?
opts: They are in a hurry or not hungry

qs.q: Which food is mentioned as a good breakfast?
What is the key point?
opts: Eat something healthy before the day starts

articles.title: Learning to Cook from Videos
body: Last year, Dewi could hardly cook anything except instant noodles. Then she found a cooking channel on the internet and decided to try one recipe every weekend.
At first, she made many mistakes. Her rice was too soft and her soup was too salty. But she kept watching the videos and took notes about what went wrong.
Now Dewi cooks dinner for her family twice a week. She says that the videos taught her more than the dishes: she learned to be patient and to try again when something fails.

qs.q: What could Dewi cook last year?
What mistake did she make at first?
What did she learn besides cooking?

articles.title: A Job Interview Gone Right
body: Rudi was very nervous before his first job interview. He had prepared his answers, but his hands were shaking when he entered the room.
The interviewer asked, "Why do you want to work for us?" Rudi took a deep breath and said, "I have followed your company for two years, and I like how you help small businesses."
The interviewer smiled. After thirty minutes, she told him that they would call him within a week. Three days later, Rudi got the call: he had the job.

qs.q: How did Rudi feel before the interview?
What did Rudi say about the company?
opts: He has followed it for two years

qs.q: What happened three days later?

articles.title: The Power of Habit
body: Researchers estimate that roughly forty percent of our daily actions are not decisions but habits. We brush our teeth, check our phones and take the same route to work without really thinking about it.

A habit usually has three parts: a cue, a routine and a reward. For example, feeling stressed (the cue) may lead to eating snacks (the routine), which gives a moment of comfort (the reward). Understanding this loop is the first step to changing it.

Experts advise against trying to remove a bad habit completely. It is easier to keep the same cue and reward but replace the routine, such as going for a short walk instead of eating snacks. Small, repeated changes usually work better than dramatic promises.

qs.q: What share of daily actions are habits?
What are the three parts of a habit?
What do experts suggest?
opts: Replace the routine, keep the cue and reward

articles.title: Is Social Media Making Us Lonely?
body: Social media promises to connect us, yet many users report feeling lonelier than before. Researchers suggest that the problem is not the technology itself but the way we use it.

Scrolling through other people's best moments can make our own lives seem dull by comparison. Moreover, a quick "like" is not the same as a real conversation. Without face-to-face contact, relationships may become shallow.

That said, social media also helps people find communities that they could never meet in person, such as patients with rare illnesses. The most sensible approach seems to be balance: use it to start conversations, then continue them offline.

qs.q: What do researchers say is the problem?
opts: The way we use social media

qs.q: Why can scrolling make life look dull?
opts: We compare ourselves with others' best moments

qs.q: What approach is suggested?

articles.title: Why Cities Are Getting Hotter
body: On a summer afternoon, a city can be several degrees warmer than the countryside around it. Scientists call this the urban heat island effect.

Concrete, asphalt and glass absorb the sun's heat during the day and release it slowly at night. With fewer trees, there is also less shade and less water vapor to cool the air. Air conditioners add to the problem by pushing hot air outside.

Fortunately, solutions exist. Planting trees, painting roofs white and building more parks can lower temperatures noticeably. Several cities have already shown that a few degrees of cooling can reduce both energy use and heat-related illness.

qs.q: What is the urban heat island effect?
opts: Cities are warmer than nearby countryside

qs.q: Why do concrete and asphalt heat cities?
opts: They absorb heat and release it slowly

qs.q: Which is a suggested solution?

articles.title: The Value of Doing Nothing
body: In a world that rewards constant activity, doing nothing feels almost guilty. Yet psychologists increasingly argue that idle time is essential for creativity and mental health.

When we stop concentrating on a task, the brain does not switch off. Instead, it begins to connect ideas that seemed unrelated, which is why solutions often appear in the shower or on a walk. Boredom, in small doses, can even push us to invent new things.

This does not mean that we should avoid work. It means that scheduling short pauses, without phones or tasks, may make us more productive in the long run. A rested mind usually works faster than a tired one.

qs.q: What do psychologists increasingly argue?
opts: Idle time is essential for creativity
Work is a waste of time

qs.q: What does the brain do when we stop concentrating?
What do short pauses do?
opts: They may make us more productive
